name: Tomato
description: Warm-season fruiting nightshade. Provide cages or stakes for support and consistent watering to prevent blossom-end rot.
water: Deep, consistent watering at soil level
healthBenefits: Rich in vitamin C, potassium, and folate
High in lycopene, a carotenoid antioxidant

warnings.text: Leaves, stems, and unripe green fruit contain tomatine/solanine; toxic to dogs and cats (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Roma
varieties.description: Determinate plum/paste tomato with dense, low-seed flesh ideal for sauces.

varieties.name: Cherokee Purple
varieties.description: Indeterminate heirloom beefsteak with dusky rose-purple skin and rich flavor.

varieties.name: Sungold
varieties.description: Vigorous indeterminate orange cherry tomato known for very sweet fruit.

varieties.name: Better Boy
varieties.description: Reliable hybrid indeterminate slicer with broad disease resistance.

name: Bell Pepper
description: Warm-season sweet pepper that ripens from green to red, yellow, or orange. Needs warm soil above 65°F.
healthBenefits: Very high in vitamin C and vitamin A (especially red ripe peppers)
Good source of vitamin B6 and dietary fiber

warnings.text: Foliage and stems contain small amounts of solanine; keep pets from chewing plants.

varieties.name: California Wonder
varieties.description: Classic heirloom 4-lobed blocky bell ripening from green to red.

varieties.name: King of the North
varieties.description: Early-maturing bell suited to cooler northern summers.

varieties.name: Golden Calwonder
varieties.description: Sweet golden-yellow bell pepper with thick walls.

name: Hot Pepper
description: Heat-loving chili peppers ranging from mild jalapeños to fiery habaneros. Thrives in beds and containers.
water: Moderate; let top inch dry slightly
healthBenefits: Rich in vitamin C and vitamin A
Contains capsaicin, studied for metabolic and pain-relief properties

warnings.text: Capsaicin oils irritate eyes and skin; wear gloves when cutting hot varieties.
Spicy fruit and foliage can cause severe GI upset in pets.

varieties.name: Jalapeño
varieties.description: Medium-heat, thick-walled chili popular fresh or pickled (2,500-8,000 SHU).

varieties.name: Serrano
varieties.description: Crisp, bright-heat chili hotter than jalapeño (10,000-23,000 SHU).

varieties.name: Habanero
varieties.description: Very hot, fruity lantern-shaped chili needing a long warm season.

name: Carrot
description: Cool-season root crop needing loose, rock-free soil for straight roots. Direct sow; does not transplant well.
water: Keep seedbed constantly moist until germination
healthBenefits: Excellent source of beta-carotene (vitamin A precursor) for eye health
Provides dietary fiber and vitamin K

varieties.name: Nantes
varieties.description: Sweet, cylindrical, blunt-tipped 6-inch carrot; great in raised beds.

varieties.name: Danvers 126
varieties.description: Sturdy tapered heirloom that tolerates heavier soils.

varieties.name: Paris Market
varieties.description: Round, golf-ball sized carrot ideal for shallow beds and containers.

name: Lettuce
description: Fast-growing cool-season salad green. Bolts quickly in summer heat; plant in spring and fall or under light shade.
healthBenefits: Hydrating low-calorie leafy green with vitamin K, vitamin A, and folate
Darker red/romaine varieties offer higher antioxidant levels

varieties.name: Buttercrunch
varieties.description: Tender, sweet butterhead with slow-bolting heat tolerance.

varieties.name: Black Seeded Simpson
varieties.description: Fast loose-leaf variety ready for cut-and-come-again harvest.

varieties.name: Parris Island Cos
varieties.description: Crisp, upright romaine with creamy hearts.

name: Spinach
description: Cold-hardy leafy green thriving in cool spring and autumn weather; bolts quickly once day length and heat rise.
healthBenefits: Nutrient-dense source of iron, folate, vitamin K, vitamin A, and lutein

warnings.text: High in oxalates; people prone to calcium-oxalate kidney stones may moderate intake.

varieties.name: Bloomsdale Long Standing
varieties.description: Savoyed heirloom with deep-green crinkly leaves and rich flavor.

varieties.name: Space
varieties.description: Smooth-leaf hybrid that is easy to wash and slow to bolt.

varieties.name: Giant Winter
varieties.description: Extra cold-hardy variety suited for fall and overwintering.

name: Kale
description: Very hardy brassica whose flavor sweetens after light autumn frosts. Productive across multiple seasons.
healthBenefits: Exceptionally rich in vitamins K, A, and C plus calcium and fiber

varieties.name: Lacinato (Dinosaur)
varieties.description: Dark blue-green savoyed Tuscan kale with tender, sweet leaves.

varieties.name: Winterbor
varieties.description: Frilly, ultra-hardy curled kale that survives heavy frost.

varieties.name: Red Russian
varieties.description: Tender oak-leaf shaped foliage with purple stems; great raw.

name: Broccoli
description: Cool-season brassica producing a large central crown followed by side shoots. Needs rich, nitrogen-adequate soil.
healthBenefits: Rich in vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, and sulforaphane glucosinolates

varieties.name: Calabrese
varieties.description: Heirloom Italian variety producing generous side shoots after main head.

varieties.name: Waltham 29
varieties.description: Cold-tolerant variety prized for fall harvests.

varieties.name: De Cicco
varieties.description: Early, prolific sprouting broccoli for continuous picking.

edibleParts: Flower heads, stems, and young leaves

name: Cabbage
description: Cool-season heading brassica. Protect young transplants with row cover against cabbage moths.
water: Even moisture to prevent head splitting
healthBenefits: Good source of vitamin C, vitamin K, and fiber; anthocyanins in red varieties

varieties.name: Golden Acre
varieties.description: Compact early green cabbage suited to smaller beds.

varieties.name: Red Acre
varieties.description: Tight, crisp reddish-purple heads with good storage life.

varieties.name: Savoy Ace
varieties.description: Tender, crinkled leaves with mild sweet flavor.

name: Cauliflower
description: Cool-season brassica that prefers steady mild temperatures; blanch white heads by tying outer leaves over the curd.
healthBenefits: Low-calorie source of vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, and choline

varieties.name: Snowball Self-Blanching
varieties.description: Classic white head whose inner leaves curl over the curd.

varieties.name: Cheddar
varieties.description: Vibrant orange curd higher in beta-carotene.

varieties.name: Graffiti
varieties.description: Deep purple cauliflower rich in anthocyanins.

name: Cucumber
description: Warm-season vining or bush cucurbit. Train vining types up a trellis to save bed space and keep fruit clean.
water: Consistent deep moisture; bitter fruit if drought-stressed
healthBenefits: High water content for hydration; provides vitamin K and trace potassium

varieties.name: Marketmore 76
varieties.description: Dark-green slicing cucumber with strong disease resistance.

varieties.name: Boston Pickling
varieties.description: Prolific heirloom crisp pickling cucumber.

varieties.name: Bush Champion
varieties.description: Compact bush habit ideal for small beds and containers.

name: Zucchini (Summer Squash)
description: Prolific warm-season bush squash. Harvest young at 6-8 inches for best flavor and continued production.
water: Deep watering at the base to avoid powdery mildew
healthBenefits: Low-calorie source of vitamin C, potassium, manganese, and vitamin B6

warnings.text: Prickly stems and leaves can irritate sensitive skin; wear sleeves when harvesting.

varieties.name: Black Beauty
varieties.description: Classic glossy dark-green heirloom zucchini.

varieties.name: Costata Romanesco
varieties.description: Ribbed Italian heirloom prized for nutty flavor and large edible blossoms.

varieties.name: Golden Zucchini
varieties.description: Bright yellow tender fruit that is easy to spot under leaves.

name: Winter Squash & Pumpkin
description: Long-season vining squash harvested with hard rinds for months of winter storage. Needs generous space or sturdy trellis.
healthBenefits: High in beta-carotene (vitamin A), vitamin C, potassium, and fiber; seeds supply magnesium and zinc

warnings.text: Coarse prickly vines can scratch skin during harvest.

varieties.name: Waltham Butternut
varieties.description: Sweet, nutty tan squash with thick necks and long storage life.

varieties.name: Sugar Pie Pumpkin
varieties.description: Small, sweet, fine-grained baking pumpkin.

varieties.name: Table Queen Acorn
varieties.description: Compact dark-green ribbed acorn squash.

name: Bush Bean
description: Compact, no-trellis snap bean that fixes atmospheric nitrogen in soil. Great for succession planting.
healthBenefits: Good source of plant protein, fiber, folate, vitamin C, and vitamin K

warnings.text: Raw mature bean seeds contain phytohemagglutinin (lectin); cook dried beans thoroughly.

varieties.name: Provider
varieties.description: Early, cold-soil-tolerant green snap bean with high yields.

varieties.name: Contender
varieties.description: Heat-tolerant stringless bush bean.

varieties.name: Royal Burgundy
varieties.description: Purple-podded snap bean that turns bright green when cooked.

name: Pole Bean
description: Climbing snap bean needing a 6-8 ft trellis or corn stalks. Produces continuously until frost.
healthBenefits: Provides fiber, folate, vitamin C, and plant protein

warnings.text: Do not eat raw mature dried beans; soak and boil thoroughly.

varieties.name: Kentucky Wonder
varieties.description: Classic meaty heirloom pole bean with rich flavor.

varieties.name: Blue Lake Pole
varieties.description: Tender, stringless straight pods ideal for fresh eating and canning.

varieties.name: Scarlet Runner
varieties.description: Ornamental red blossoms that attract hummingbirds plus edible pods.

name: Garden Pea
description: Cool-season nitrogen-fixing climber planted as soon as soil can be worked in early spring. Provide low netting.
healthBenefits: Rich in plant protein, vitamin C, vitamin K, manganese, and dietary fiber

varieties.name: Sugar Snap
varieties.description: Plump, crisp, sweet edible-pod climbing pea.

varieties.name: Oregon Sugar Pod II
varieties.description: Disease-resistant flat snow pea for stir-fries.

varieties.name: Little Marvel
varieties.description: Compact dwarf shelling pea needing minimal staking.

name: Sweet Corn
description: Wind-pollinated warm-season grain. Plant in blocks of at least 4×4 plants rather than a single row for full ears.
healthBenefits: Provides dietary fiber, B vitamins (thiamine, folate), and lutein/zeaxanthin

varieties.name: Golden Bantam
varieties.description: Historic yellow heirloom with rich old-fashioned corn flavor.

varieties.name: Silver Queen
varieties.description: Late-season sweet white hybrid with tender kernels.

varieties.name: Peaches and Cream
varieties.description: Popular bicolor early-mid sweet corn.

name: Potato
description: Cool-season tuber crop grown from certified seed potatoes. Hill soil or straw around stems to prevent greening.
healthBenefits: Rich in potassium, vitamin C, vitamin B6, and resistant starch when cooled

warnings.text: Green potato skins, sprouts, leaves, and stems contain toxic solanine; never eat green parts.
Raw green potatoes and potato foliage are toxic to dogs and cats (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Yukon Gold
varieties.description: Buttery yellow-fleshed all-purpose early-mid potato.

varieties.name: Red Norland
varieties.description: Early red-skinned boiling and roasting potato.

varieties.name: Russet Burbank
varieties.description: Classic late-season baking and frying potato.

name: Sweet Potato
description: Heat-loving trailing vine grown from slips after soil is thoroughly warm. Tolerates summer heat well.
healthBenefits: Exceptional source of beta-carotene (vitamin A), vitamin C, potassium, and fiber

varieties.name: Beauregard
varieties.description: High-yielding copper-skinned variety with deep orange flesh.

varieties.name: Georgia Jet
varieties.description: Fast-maturing variety suited to shorter northern summers.

varieties.name: Stokes Purple
varieties.description: Rich purple flesh high in anthocyanins.

name: Onion
description: Cool-season allium. Choose day-length type for your latitude (long-day north, intermediate mid, short-day south).
water: Shallow regular watering; stop when tops fall
healthBenefits: Contains quercetin (antioxidant flavonoid), prebiotic fructans, and vitamin C

warnings.text: All parts of onion are toxic to dogs and cats; can cause hemolytic anemia (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Walla Walla Sweet
varieties.description: Large, mild, sweet long-day onion.

varieties.name: Red Creole
varieties.description: Pungent short-day red storage onion for southern zones.

varieties.name: Evergreen White Bunching
varieties.description: Non-bulbing green scallion ready in ~65 days.

name: Garlic
description: Hardy allium typically planted in autumn for summer harvest. Hardneck types excel in cold zones; softneck in mild zones.
water: Moderate spring moisture; dry off before harvest
healthBenefits: Contains allicin and organosulfur compounds studied for cardiovascular support

warnings.text: Garlic is strongly toxic to dogs and cats; causes red blood cell damage (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Music (Hardneck)
varieties.description: Large, easy-to-peel cold-hardy porcelain cloves with rich heat.

varieties.name: Inchelium Red (Softneck)
varieties.description: Vigorous, mild-flavored braiding garlic with long storage.

varieties.name: Chesnok Red (Hardneck)
varieties.description: Purple-stripe heirloom prized for sweet roasted flavor.

name: Leek
description: Mild, sweet allium. Plant deeply in trenches and hill soil around stems for long white shanks.
healthBenefits: Source of vitamin K, manganese, vitamin A, and prebiotic inulin

warnings.text: Allium species — toxic to dogs and cats (ASPCA).

varieties.name: King Richard
varieties.description: Early, tall, tender summer leek.

varieties.name: American Flag
varieties.description: Classic heirloom winter-hardy leek with thick shanks.

edibleParts: Blanched white stalk and light-green leaves

name: Radish
description: Fastest-maturing garden vegetable — ready in 3-4 weeks. Great intercrop and row-marker for slow-germinating carrots.
water: Even moisture to prevent pithy or overly hot roots
healthBenefits: Crisp low-calorie source of vitamin C and antioxidants

varieties.name: Cherry Belle
varieties.description: Bright red round radish ready in ~22 days.

varieties.name: French Breakfast
varieties.description: Elongated red-and-white mild crisp heirloom.

varieties.name: Watermelon Radish
varieties.description: Heirloom fall daikon with sweet magenta interior.

name: Beet
description: Dual-purpose cool-season crop: harvest both tender tops and sweet earthy roots. Thin multigerm seed clusters to one seedling.
healthBenefits: High in folate, manganese, dietary nitrates (vascular support), and betalain pigments

warnings.text: Beet greens are high in oxalates; harmless red coloration of urine (beeturia) is common.

varieties.name: Detroit Dark Red
varieties.description: Smooth, deep-red heirloom root great for roasting and canning.

varieties.name: Chioggia
varieties.description: Italian heirloom with striking red-and-white candy-stripe rings.

varieties.name: Touchstone Gold
varieties.description: Sweet golden-orange beet that does not stain.

name: Eggplant
description: Heat-loving nightshade requiring warm nights and fertile soil. Protect young plants from flea beetles.
healthBenefits: Provides dietary fiber, manganese, and nasunin (an antioxidant in purple skin)

warnings.text: Leaves and stems contain solanine; keep pets away from foliage (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Black Beauty
varieties.description: Classic glossy deep-purple globe heirloom.

varieties.name: Ichiban
varieties.description: Slender, tender Japanese eggplant with thin skin and early harvest.

varieties.name: Patio Baby
varieties.description: Compact dwarf variety yielding mini fruits in containers.

name: Swiss Chard
description: Heat-tolerant relative of beets that produces vibrant, cut-and-come-again greens from spring through hard frost.
healthBenefits: Very rich in vitamins K, A, and C plus magnesium, potassium, and iron

warnings.text: High in oxalates; cooking reduces soluble oxalate content.

varieties.name: Bright Lights
varieties.description: Rainbow mix of gold, pink, orange, crimson, and white stems.

varieties.name: Fordhook Giant
varieties.description: Vigorous heirloom with broad white stalks and dark crinkly leaves.

name: Celery
description: Long-season moisture-loving cool crop. Needs rich composted soil and steady water for crisp, tender stalks.
water: Consistently moist soil; never let dry out
healthBenefits: Low-calorie source of vitamin K, potassium, folate, and apigenin antioxidants

warnings.text: Celery is a recognized food allergen for some individuals.

varieties.name: Utah 52-70
varieties.description: Tall, crisp, dark-green standard garden celery.

varieties.name: Tango
varieties.description: Heat-tolerant, smooth-stalked hybrid easier for home gardeners.

name: Turnip
description: Fast, cold-hardy root and green crop. Best grown in spring or fall when cool temperatures keep roots sweet.
healthBenefits: Roots provide vitamin C and fiber; turnip greens are rich in vitamins K, A, and calcium

varieties.name: Purple Top White Globe
varieties.description: Classic white root with rosy-purple shoulders.

varieties.name: Hakurei (Tokyo)
varieties.description: Tender, sweet white salad turnip delicious raw in ~38 days.

name: Asparagus
description: Long-lived perennial vegetable (15-20+ years). Allow crowns to establish 1-2 years before full spring harvests.
healthBenefits: Rich in folate, vitamin K, vitamin C, and prebiotic fiber

warnings.text: Asparagus fern foliage and berries are toxic to dogs and cats (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Mary Washington
varieties.description: Classic rust-resistant heirloom variety.

varieties.name: Jersey Knight
varieties.description: All-male hybrid prized for heavy yields of thick spears.

name: Okra
description: Tall heat-loving summer vegetable related to hibiscus. Harvest pods frequently at 3-4 inches before they turn woody.
healthBenefits: Good source of vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, and soluble mucilage fiber

warnings.text: Fine hairs on stems and pods can cause itching; wear gloves when harvesting.

varieties.name: Clemson Spineless
varieties.description: All-America classic with straight, spineless dark-green pods.

varieties.name: Burgundy
varieties.description: Ornamental deep-red pods and stems that turn green when cooked.

name: Basil
description: Warm-season aromatic culinary herb. Pinch growing tips and flower buds regularly to keep plants bushy.
healthBenefits: Rich in vitamin K and aromatic essential oils with antioxidant properties

varieties.name: Genovese
varieties.description: Classic large-leaf Italian sweet basil for pesto.

varieties.name: Siam Queen Thai
varieties.description: Spicy anise-clove flavor with purple stems and blooms.

varieties.name: Dark Opal
varieties.description: Deep purple ornamental and culinary leaves.

name: Dill
description: Cool-to-warm aromatic annual that attracts beneficial lacewings, ladybugs, and swallowtail caterpillars.
healthBenefits: Source of vitamin A, vitamin C, and manganese; seeds traditionally used as a digestive herb

varieties.name: Bouquet
varieties.description: Tall early-flowering variety ideal for pickling.

varieties.name: Fernleaf
varieties.description: Compact 18-inch dwarf dill suited to containers and square-foot beds.

name: Parsley
description: Biennial culinary herb grown as an annual in cold zones. Slow to germinate (2-4 weeks); soak seeds overnight.
healthBenefits: Exceptionally rich in vitamin K, vitamin C, vitamin A, and apigenin

warnings.text: Spring parsley (large amounts) can cause photosensitivity in pets; culinary parsley is mild (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Italian Giant Flat-Leaf
varieties.description: Bold, sweet flavor preferred for cooking.

varieties.name: Triple Curled
varieties.description: Dense, decorative ruffled foliage great for garnishes.

name: Cilantro (Coriander)
description: Fast cool-season annual herb that bolts quickly in summer heat. Sow small batches every 2-3 weeks.
healthBenefits: Provides vitamins K, A, and C plus dietary antioxidants

varieties.name: Santo
varieties.description: Slow-bolting selection bred for abundant leaf production.

varieties.name: Calypso
varieties.description: One of the slowest-bolting varieties for warm spring beds.

name: Mint
description: Vigorous perennial herb that spreads rapidly by underground runners. Best grown in containers to prevent takeover.
healthBenefits: Contains menthol and rosmarinic acid; traditionally used to soothe digestion

warnings.text: Spreads aggressively via rhizomes; plant in pots or sunken barriers.
Garden mint in large quantities (and especially pennyroyal) can upset dogs and cats (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Spearmint
varieties.description: Classic sweet, mild culinary mint for teas and cooking.

varieties.name: Peppermint
varieties.description: Strong, cooling menthol aroma ideal for herbal tea.

varieties.name: Chocolate Mint
varieties.description: Dark stems with subtle cocoa-mint fragrance.

name: Rosemary
description: Woody, drought-tolerant Mediterranean perennial herb. Overwinter indoors in pots in zones 7 and colder.
healthBenefits: Contains rosmarinic and carnosic acids with antioxidant properties; aromatic culinary herb

varieties.name: Tuscan Blue
varieties.description: Upright fragrant variety with bright blue blooms.

varieties.name: Arp
varieties.description: Most cold-hardy rosemary, surviving down to Zone 6/7 with mulch.

name: Thyme
description: Low-growing woody perennial culinary herb that attracts pollinators and tolerates dry, sunny edges.
healthBenefits: Contains thymol, vitamin C, and iron; classic culinary herb

varieties.name: English Thyme
varieties.description: Classic savory broad-leaf culinary thyme.

varieties.name: Lemon Thyme
varieties.description: Bright citrus-scented leaves great for fish and teas.

name: Oregano
description: Hardy Mediterranean perennial herb whose flowers draw bees and hoverflies. Flavor peaks just before blooming.
healthBenefits: High in antioxidant polyphenols (carvacrol, thymol) and vitamin K

warnings.text: Concentrated oregano oil or large ingestions may cause mild GI upset in pets (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Greek Oregano
varieties.description: Intense, pungent flavor prized for Mediterranean dishes.

varieties.name: Italian Oregano
varieties.description: Milder, sweeter hybrid of oregano and marjoram.

name: Chives
description: Cold-hardy perennial allium forming neat grassy clumps with edible lavender-pink pom-pom flowers in spring.
healthBenefits: Provides vitamin K, vitamin C, and mild allium sulfur compounds

warnings.text: Allium species — toxic to dogs and cats (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Common Chives
varieties.description: Delicate onion flavor with spring purple blooms.

varieties.name: Garlic Chives
varieties.description: Flat leaves with mild garlic flavor and late-summer white flowers.

name: Sage
description: Silvery-green woody perennial herb that repels cabbage moths and thrives in dry, sunny spots.
healthBenefits: Rich in vitamin K and antioxidant phenolic compounds

varieties.name: Common Garden Sage
varieties.description: Classic velvety gray-green culinary sage.

varieties.name: Purple Sage
varieties.description: Ornamental reddish-purple foliage with milder flavor.

name: Strawberry
description: Perennial berry groundcover great for raised beds, borders, and hanging containers. Mulch with straw to keep fruit clean.
healthBenefits: High in vitamin C, manganese, folate, and anthocyanin antioxidants

varieties.name: Seascape
varieties.description: Day-neutral variety producing large sweet berries spring through fall.

varieties.name: Honeoye
varieties.description: Cold-hardy June-bearing variety with heavy early crops.

varieties.name: Alpine (Alexandria)
varieties.description: Runnerless compact heirloom with intensely aromatic small berries.

name: Raspberry
description: Perennial bramble shrub bearing sweet summer or fall berries. Support canes with simple wire trellising.
healthBenefits: Very high in dietary fiber, vitamin C, manganese, and ellagitannin antioxidants

warnings.text: Most varieties have prickly canes; wear gloves when pruning.
Spreads by root suckers; edge beds or mow around rows.

varieties.name: Heritage
varieties.description: Reliable primocane (fall-bearing) red raspberry; easy annual mowing.

varieties.name: Anne
varieties.description: Large, sweet golden-yellow fall-bearing raspberry.

name: Blueberry (Bush)
description: Acid-loving perennial berry shrub (pH 4.5-5.5). Plant at least two varieties for better cross-pollination and yields.
water: Consistent shallow moisture; acidic pine-bark mulch
healthBenefits: Packed with anthocyanins, vitamin C, vitamin K, and manganese

varieties.name: Bluecrop
varieties.description: Mid-season northern highbush prized for dependable heavy crops.

varieties.name: Top Hat
varieties.description: Compact 2-foot dwarf bush ideal for patio containers.

name: Blackberry
description: Vigorous perennial bramble shrub. Choose modern thornless varieties for easy picking in home gardens.
healthBenefits: High in fiber, vitamin C, vitamin K, and dark anthocyanin antioxidants

warnings.text: Thorny varieties have sharp prickles; choose thornless cultivars like Triple Crown for family yards.

varieties.name: Triple Crown
varieties.description: Thornless semi-erect variety with large, sweet berries.

varieties.name: Baby Cakes
varieties.description: Compact thornless dwarf blackberry bred for patio pots.

name: Watermelon
description: Heat-loving sprawling vine needing warm soil and generous sunlight. Icebox varieties fit smaller gardens or trellises.
water: Deep watering while vines grow; reduce slightly as fruit ripens
healthBenefits: Hydrating fruit rich in lycopene, citrulline, vitamin A, and vitamin C

varieties.name: Sugar Baby
varieties.description: Compact 8-10 lb icebox melon with sweet deep-red flesh.

varieties.name: Crimson Sweet
varieties.description: Classic 20-25 lb striped heirloom with high sugar content.

name: Cantaloupe (Muskmelon)
description: Warm-season sweet melon harvested at 'full slip' when stem detaches cleanly with light thumb pressure.
healthBenefits: Excellent source of beta-carotene (vitamin A), vitamin C, and potassium

varieties.name: Hale's Best Jumbo
varieties.description: Fragrant, sweet orange-fleshed heirloom melon.

varieties.name: Minnesota Midget
varieties.description: Compact 3-foot vines producing personal-size melons early.

name: Marigold
description: Bright, easy annual companion flower that attracts pollinators and helps deter root-knot nematodes and garden pests.
healthBenefits: Attracts beneficial hoverflies, ladybugs, and pollinators to vegetable beds

warnings.text: Foliage sap may cause mild skin irritation in sensitive individuals.

varieties.name: French Marigold
varieties.description: Compact, bushy variety best studied for nematode suppression.

varieties.name: Crackerjack African
varieties.description: Tall showy blooms in bright gold, orange, and yellow.

name: Sunflower
description: Iconic annual flower drawing bees and songbirds. Tall types act as living trellises; dwarf types fit beds and pots.
healthBenefits: Seeds are rich in vitamin E, healthy unsaturated fats, magnesium, and selenium

warnings.text: Allelopathic seed hulls and roots can inhibit nearby sensitive seedlings like potatoes.

varieties.name: Mammoth Russian
varieties.description: Towering 8-12 ft classic producing large edible seed heads.

varieties.name: Teddy Bear
varieties.description: Fluffy 2-3 ft dwarf golden blooms great for containers.

varieties.name: Autumn Beauty
varieties.description: Multi-branching bronze, gold, and mahogany cut flowers.

name: Zinnia
description: Heat-loving cut-and-come-again annual that blooms nonstop until frost and acts as a magnet for butterflies.
water: Water at soil level to reduce powdery mildew
healthBenefits: Top nectar plant for monarch butterflies, swallowtails, and native bees

varieties.name: Benary's Giant
varieties.description: Tall, sturdy stems with large dahlia-like cut blooms.

varieties.name: Profusion
varieties.description: Compact, mildew-resistant mounding zinnia for borders.

name: Nasturtium
description: Peppery edible flower that thrives in lean soil and serves as a classic trap crop for aphids and squash bugs.
water: Low to moderate; avoid rich fertilizer
healthBenefits: Edible peppery leaves and blossoms supply vitamin C and lutein

varieties.name: Jewel Mix
varieties.description: Compact bush variety in red, orange, and gold.

varieties.name: Alaska
varieties.description: Variegated cream-and-green leaves with bright blooms.

edibleParts: Leaves, flowers, and young seed pods

name: Lavender
description: Fragrant, drought-tolerant Mediterranean perennial subshrub that draws bumblebees and resists deer.
healthBenefits: Aromatic flowers widely used in relaxation teas and aromatherapy; major pollinator plant

warnings.text: Contains linalool and linalyl acetate; can cause nausea in dogs and cats if eaten in quantity (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Munstead
varieties.description: Compact, cold-hardy English lavender suited for culinary use.

varieties.name: Hidcote
varieties.description: Deep violet-blue flower spikes with silvery foliage.

name: Echinacea (Coneflower)
description: Tough North American native perennial with daisy-like blooms; leave seed heads up in fall for goldfinches.
healthBenefits: Supports native bees, butterflies, and seed-eating songbirds; traditionally studied as an herbal tea

warnings.text: Member of the Asteraceae (ragweed) family; may trigger allergies in sensitive individuals.

varieties.name: Purple Coneflower (Magnus)
varieties.description: Classic rosy-purple petals around a spiky copper cone.

varieties.name: Cheyenne Spirit
varieties.description: First-year blooming mix in scarlet, orange, yellow, and purple.

name: Cosmos
description: Airy, lacy-foliage annual that thrives in poor dry soil and attracts parasitic wasps, lacewings, and butterflies.
healthBenefits: Draws beneficial predatory insects and pollinators throughout summer

varieties.name: Sensation Mix
varieties.description: Tall 3-4 ft blooms in pink, magenta, and white.

varieties.name: Bright Lights (Sulfur)
varieties.description: Fiery orange-yellow heat-tolerant blooms.

name: Tulip
description: Classic spring-blooming bulb planted in autumn for vibrant early-season color.
water: Moderate in spring; dry in summer dormancy
healthBenefits: Early spring nectar source and cheerful seasonal color

warnings.text: Bulbs (highest concentration) and foliage contain tulipalin; toxic to dogs and cats (ASPCA).
Handling many bulbs can cause contact dermatitis ('tulip fingers').

varieties.name: Darwin Hybrid
varieties.description: Large, sturdy classic goblet blooms that perennialize well.

varieties.name: Queen of Night
varieties.description: Dramatic velvety maroon-black late-spring tulip.

name: Rose (Shrub)
description: Classic flowering shrub. Choose disease-resistant landscape varieties for low-maintenance beds.
healthBenefits: Unsprayed rose hips are rich in vitamin C; fragrant blooms support garden enjoyment

warnings.text: Sharp thorns on canes; wear heavy leather gloves when pruning.

varieties.name: Knock Out Shrub
varieties.description: Ultra-hardy, black-spot-resistant repeat bloomer.

varieties.name: Rosa Rugosa
varieties.description: Fragrant salt-tolerant shrub producing large vitamin-rich rose hips.

name: Hosta
description: Lush shade-loving foliage perennial ideal for woodland borders and north-facing garden beds.
healthBenefits: Provides cool shade groundcover and suppresses weeds under shaded borders

warnings.text: Contains saponins; toxic to dogs and cats, causing vomiting and diarrhea (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Patriot
varieties.description: Dark-green leaves with crisp wide white margins.

varieties.name: Blue Angel
varieties.description: Large, heavily textured blue-green foliage.

name: Fountain Grass
description: Graceful arching ornamental grass with feathery bottlebrush plumes that add late-season movement and texture.
healthBenefits: Provides winter shelter for beneficial insects and birds

warnings.text: Some non-sterile Pennisetum cultivars can self-seed aggressively in mild zones; choose sterile selections.

varieties.name: Hameln (Dwarf)
varieties.description: Compact 2-3 ft clump with creamy plumes.

varieties.name: Little Bunny
varieties.description: Miniature 12-18 inch grass ideal for borders and pots.

name: Peony
description: Long-lived herbaceous perennial with lush spring blooms. Plant eyes no deeper than 1-2 inches below soil surface.
healthBenefits: Decades-long perennial focal point; fragrant blooms attract pollinators

warnings.text: Contains paeonol (especially in bark/roots); toxic to dogs and cats (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Sarah Bernhardt
varieties.description: Fragrant double apple-blossom pink heirloom.

varieties.name: Festiva Maxima
varieties.description: Large fragrant double white blooms with crimson flecks.

name: Creeping Thyme
description: Fragrant, walkable low mat (2-3 inches tall) ideal between pavers and along bed edges; blankets in pink-purple blooms.
healthBenefits: Living mulch that cools soil, suppresses weeds, and feeds honeybees

varieties.name: Elfin
varieties.description: Ultra-low 1-2 inch cushion thyme perfect between stepping stones.

varieties.name: Red Creeping (Coccineus)
varieties.description: Vivid magenta-red summer flower carpet.

name: White Clover
description: Nitrogen-fixing living mulch for pathways and berry aisles. Stays green in drought and feeds native bees.
healthBenefits: Fixes atmospheric nitrogen naturally and supports honeybees and bumblebees

warnings.text: Spreads by stolons into adjacent beds if not edged.

varieties.name: Dutch White
varieties.description: Classic low-growing pathway and lawn clover.

varieties.name: Microclover
varieties.description: Extra-fine dwarf leaves forming a dense green carpet.

name: Sweet Alyssum
description: Honey-scented low edging annual that blooms non-stop and recruits hoverflies and parasitic wasps to control aphids.
healthBenefits: Premier insectary border plant for natural biological aphid control

varieties.name: Carpet of Snow
varieties.description: Crisp fragrant white 4-inch flower carpet.

varieties.name: Royal Carpet
varieties.description: Rich violet-purple fragrant edging.

name: Grapevine
description: Woody perennial fruiting vine requiring a sturdy trellis or arbor and annual late-winter pruning.
healthBenefits: Provides vitamin K, vitamin C, and resveratrol polyphenols in dark skins

warnings.text: Grapes and raisins can cause acute kidney failure in dogs — keep vines inaccessible to dogs (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Concord
varieties.description: Cold-hardy slip-skin blue-black grape for juice and jelly.

varieties.name: Reliance Seedless
varieties.description: Sweet pink seedless table grape hardy to Zone 4.

name: Clematis
description: Flowering perennial climbing vine. Famous rule: 'head in the sun, feet in the shade' — mulch or shade the root zone.
healthBenefits: Vertical nectar source and dramatic climbing color on trellises and fences

warnings.text: Contains protoanemonin; toxic to dogs and cats, causing salivation and GI upset (ASPCA).
Sap can irritate skin; wear gloves when pruning.

varieties.name: Jackmanii
varieties.description: Prolific deep velvety purple summer-blooming classic.

varieties.name: Nelly Moser
varieties.description: Large pale-pink blooms with carmine bars; tolerates part shade.

name: Sweet Pea
description: Fragrant cool-season ornamental climbing annual prized for pastel cut flowers in spring.
healthBenefits: Intensely fragrant cut flower attracting spring pollinators

warnings.text: NOT edible — ornamental Lathyrus odoratus seeds are toxic to humans if ingested (unlike garden peas).
Seeds and stems are toxic to dogs, cats, and horses (ASPCA).

varieties.name: Royal Family Mix
varieties.description: Heat-tolerant long-stemmed fragrant pastel blooms.

varieties.name: Cupani
varieties.description: Historic heirloom with deep purple-maroon blooms and intense scent.
